The self-belief is operationally an expectation about this exercise's observed
performance. “Insecure” and “confident” mean low/high expected success here. The
experiment does not identify a latent competence parameter from results, calibrate
probability of correctness, or supply a general distinction between competence belief
and a separately composed current-outcome predictor. Changing difficulty or impairment
